newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to set daily baht-dlr rate from July 3.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to set daily baht-dlr rate from July 3.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Wednesday that it would set the much-awaited daily baht-dollar reference rate from Thursday (July 3) following the currency's flotation.
The rate, based on the baht's trading average the day before, would be published around 8.30 a.m. or 0130 GMT daily, a Bank of Thailand official told Reuters.
The official said the rate would be based on the baht-dollar trading average of the previous day based on the "counter rate" which is the exchange rate banks charge their customers.

Thailand on Wednesday stunned markets by abruptly changing its baht system and saying it would allow the currency to float and that the currency's value would be determined by market forces. The baht initially plunged to a record low of around 29.00 baht on the news but later steadied and pared losses.

The central bank had also said that it had an "appropriate rate" in mind in which it expected the baht to move. The authorities also warned that the central bank would intervene from time to time to achieve its baht policy objectives.

Traders said that with the new reference rate setting, it would be extremely hard to make assumptions on where the baht was heading. It was easier under the previous system when the baht was pegged to a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar.
